items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1972-09-13
items.q: And John Sincere guitar. John Sincere guitar.

ctx.x: How did you play a five string banjo? Well, I was going from the book.

Did you play with fingers or with your pick? I played with the pick. I had a rap. How did you tune that fifth string? Well, I learned how to tune it. But you didn't have to tune it. I took that fifth string off. Oh, I see. I took it off. You know they got their four string, five string banjos. Yeah. Because we were rehearsing by... I had a little jam session by... What's that boy? That saxophone player that died? John. Hanging? John, Hanging's grubber, you know? Yeah. Yeah. You called them cash or something.…
Yeah, I see. He took that... The one off that's not fretted. Yeah, yeah. The one that's not fretted.

items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1972-09-13
items.q: Johnny Sensei was the first guy who showed me how to play the guitar.

ctx.x: That was real interesting what you were saying about Gayno.

Gayno never had a band. I was the one who knew Gayno how to play in a band. He played after me because I was probably playing this, Johnny Sensei was the first guy who showed me how to play the guitar. And then I switched from guitar to banjo. Johnny Sensei used to play with us too on the Airline Highway. In the 4900, he was on the Airline Highway. We played there. He had a little trumpet called Caledon. He said, I'll be there when you're going to get there. I said, okay. I had playing with him. I had Lawrence's…
What did he play? He played Coney. You mean the guy that was any kind of Blue? No, it wasn't a kind of Blue. No, it wasn't no kind of Blue.
